# proxmox_cluster_mapping_pci (Resource)

Manages a cluster-wide PCI hardware mapping through `/cluster/mapping/pci`, referenced by `hostpci.mapping`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "proxmox_cluster_mapping_pci" "gpu" {
  id          = "gpu-node1"
  description = "passthrough GPU"

  map = [{
    node         = "pve-1"
    path         = "0000:01:00.0"
    id           = "10de:1eb8"
    subsystem_id = "10de:12a2"
  }]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) Stable mapping identifier (`pve-configid`). Changes require replacement.
- `map` (Attributes Set) Node to PCI device mapping. Every entry needs `node`, `path` and the expected `id`; Proxmox compares them at guest start. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--map))

### Optional

- `description` (String) Mapping description.
- `live_migration_capable` (Boolean) Marks the devices as live-migratable (experimental, needs hardware and driver support).

<a id="nestedatt--map"></a>
### Nested Schema for `map`

Required:

- `id` (String) Expected vendor:device id (`VVVV:DDDD`), used to detect hardware changes.
- `node` (String) Cluster node the map entry belongs to.
- `path` (String) PCI address (`bus:dev.func`), optionally a semicolon separated list of alternatives.

Optional:

- `description` (String) Node specific device description.
- `iommugroup` (Number) Expected IOMMU group, used to detect hardware changes.
- `subsystem_id` (String) Expected subsystem vendor:device id (`VVVV:DDDD`).
